The delay is likely caused by crash. On my PC, I see output below.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8bac748-8979-4307-a5e6-0357e02efda3)

Also applies in v4.4.beta.custom_build [06acfccf8]

Reduced it to an MRP: [AetherNightsMRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18718490/AetherNightsMRP.zip)

The issue occurs when assigning a lambda to a static variable of another script. If the script from which the lambda originates does not have any static variables it will be freed as soon as it is no longer used (main scene is destructed). ~When that is the case it frees the UpdatableFunctionPtr of the lambda. When the script with the static variable gets destructed afterwards it clears its static variables and tries to destruct the UpdatableFunctionPtr again.~ When that is the case it will clear the list of updatable function pointers. Since each update function pointer keeps a pointer to its list element, this will lead to an exception if the function pointer is freed after the list is cleared, since the list element was already freed and the function pointer will try to erase it.

We could work around this by setting the element to a nullptr for all updatable function pointers, when freeing a GDScript. But in reality a updatable function pointer to a freed GDScript just seems like something that should not happen (given that the function pointers can't be invalidated to create a proper runtime error in that case). But I guess trying to introduce a ref here to prevent the gdscript from being freed would lead to other issues with cyclic references.

@tex111 to work around this for now, don't use lambdas for when you store stuff in `Game` and use member functions instead, they use a different callable implementation without a function pointer involved.

```
      x1 = 0x00000001853280ef  "recursive_mutex lock failed"
```

My guess is it's trying to access a `GDScript` after destruction.
Especially looking at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101830, which it may be related to.

> My guess is it's trying to access a `GDScript` after destruction.

Yep, that's whats happening. The script with the static variable tries to access the script from which the lambda originates (through the function pointer from how I understand it) when it gets destructed. But the script from which the lambda comes has wrongly been freed before.

Is there any chance of this getting fixed, or at least making it easier to track down where the problematic data is?

I think I've found a pretty good workaround: as long as the global class inherits from Object (**not** RefCounted!), you can make a lazy-loaded static instance and that won't have any issues:

```gdscript
class_name Game extends Object

static var instance: Game:
	get:
		if not instance:
			instance = Game.new()
		return instance

var context: Callable
```

```gdscript
extends Node


func _ready() -> void:
	Game.instance.context = func(): return
```

I think it's because since `instance` isn't collected when the Script gets destroyed, it doesn't destroy its own FuncPtrs or whatever

I just ran into this. As a part of the unloading process and cleaning up, `GDScript::~GDScript` and `GDScript::clear` does this:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1cf31805370716ce8160ddc1394b9820249a21f7/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp#L1569

Which leaves any stored `Callable`s (that use `GDScript::UpdatableFuncPtr`) in a pickle. They do not check if `ptr` is null in the destructor, which is a more accurate indication that their `script` member has become invalidated. That is the fix that I went with locally as it preserves the existing semantics. I am not fond of introducing `Ref` here or the like, non-owning weak pointers feels correct; it's just bugged.

tldr; `GDScript::UpdatableFuncPtr::~UpdatableFuncPtr` needs to return (do nothing) when its `ptr` is null.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1cf31805370716ce8160ddc1394b9820249a21f7/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp#L1522

I'm not creating a pull that does this as it seems there is no consensus on the book-keeping mechanics.
